executiveAssessment.text:
Executive Conclusion. YOTEL Geneva Lake reaches many monitored demand scenarios, but consideration consistency is the primary constraint.

What the Data Is Telling Us. Scenario Presence at 90.5% shows broad recognition across monitored traveler needs. AI Consideration at 34.9% shows that recognition does not consistently convert into selection in individual answers. The management problem is inclusion consistency — not awareness. Softness concentrates in Wellness; Business Travel and Group / Meeting remain stronger.

Why It Matters. Broad scenario reach without consistent appearance in AI answers means the hotel is known in the demand set but not reliably carried into traveler-facing answers. Management attention should start with consistency of representation, not with assuming the hotel needs an entirely new competitive set.

Where the Pattern Is Concentrated. Wellness is the softest Scenario Capture at 75.0%, while Business Travel and Group / Meeting show broader coverage. The inclusion issue is concentrated, not universal. Reality Coverage is 16.7% (1 of 6 attributes). Start with gaps that matter operationally — beginning with Pet-Friendly.

What Management Should Focus On Now. Focus first on consistency of representation for Wellness. Confirm priority sources present the same use cases and attributes that appear in scenarios where the hotel is absent, and close gaps that repeatedly coincide with cases where the hotel is missing.

What Not to Overreact To. No comparable prior official period is available — read these as current levels, not period-over-period change.

What to Review Next. Compare high-presence versus low-consideration scenarios and inspect which sources and attributes appear when the hotel is missing. Use that evidence pack before changing channel strategy.
